G3900.def:
παρά-πτωρμα, -τος, τό
(παραπίπτω), [in LXX for מַעַל, פֶּשַׁע, etc. ;] 
__1. a false step, a blunder (Polyb.). 
__2. Ethically, a misdeed, trespass (LXX): Matthieu 6:14-15, Marc 11:25-26, Romains 4:25 5:15 ff Romains 11:11-12, 2 Corinthiens 5:19, Galates 6:1, Éphésiens 1:7 2:1, 5, Colossiens 2:13.†
SYN.: see: ἁμαρτία

G3901.def:
παρα-ρρέω 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 44:4 (יָבַל), Proverbes 3:21 * ;] 
to flow by, drift away, slip away: Hébreux 2:1.†

G3902.def:
παράσημος, -ον
(σῆμα, a mark) [in LXX: 3Ma.2:29 * ;] 
__1. in cl., marked amiss, spurious, counterfeit. Later, 
__2. marked at the side, annotated (Plut.). 
__3. marked with a sign (LXX); as subst., a figure­head : Actes 28:11 (see MM, xix).†

G3903.def:
παρα-σκευάζω 
[in LXX: Jérémie 50:42 (עָרַךְ), etc. ;] 
to prepare, make ready: absol. (sc. τ. δεῖπνον, etc.; of. Hdt., ix, 82, 2Ma.2:27), Actes 10:10; mid., to prepare, make preparations: 1 Corinthiens 14:8 (cf. Je, l.with); pass., 2 Corinthiens 9:2-3.†

G3904.def:
παρα-σκευή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX: Exode 35:24 39:42 (עֲבֹדָה, with seel., ἀποσκ-, κατασκ-), Jdth.2:17 4:5, 1Ma.9:35 א, 2Ma.15:21 * ;] 
__1. preparation. 
__2. equipment (Jth, ll with). 
__3. In Jewish usage, the day of preparation for a Sabbath or a feast (= προσάββατον, which see) : Matthieu 27:62, Marc 15:42, Luc 23:54, Jean 19:31; with genitive, τοῦ πάσχα, Jean 19:14; τ. Ἰoυδαίων, Jean 19:42 (it is the name for Friday in MGr.).†

G3905.def:
παρα-τείνω 
[in LXX: Nombres 23:28 (שָׁקַף ni.), etc. ;] 
to extend, pro­long: τ. λόγον, Actes 20:7.†

G3906.def:
παρα-τηρέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Psaumes 37:12 (זָמַם), Psaumes 130:8 (שָׁמַר), Da TH Daniel 6:11 (12), Su 1:12,15,16* ;] 
__1. to watch closely, observe narrowly: so mid., τ. πύλας, Actes 9:24; with evil intent, Marc 3:2, Luc 20:20 (absol., see Field, Notes, 74); so mid., Luc 6:7 14:1. 
__2. to observe scrupulously (of days and seasons; cf. Exode 12:42, Sm.): mid., Galates 4:10.†

G3907.def:
παρα-τήρησις, -εως, ἡ 
[in Aq.: Exode 12:42 (see: παρατηρέω) * ;] 
obser­vation: Luc 17:20 (Polyb., Plut., al.).†

G3908.def:
παρα-τίθημι 
[in LXX chiefly for שׂוּם ;] 
__I. Act., to place beside, set before, with accusative and dative: of food, Marc 6:41 8:6-7, Luc 9:16 11:6; τράπεζαν, Actes 16:34; pass. ptcp., Luc 10:8, 1 Corinthiens 10:27; metaphorically, of teaching, παραβολήν, Matthieu 13:24, 31. 
__II. Mid., 
__1. to have set before one (Hom., Thuc., Xen., al.). 
__2. to deposit with another, give in charge or commit to (Hdt., Xen., Polyb., al.) : with accusative and dative, Luc 12:48 23:46, Actes 14:23 20:32, 1 Timothée 1:18, 2 Timothée 2:2, 1 Pierre 4:19. 
__3. to bring forward, quote as evidence: before ὅτι, Actes 17:3 (see Page, in l).†

G3909.def:
παρα-τυγχάνω 
to happen to be near or present: Actes 17:17.†

G3910.def:
παρ-αυτίκα
adv. (πάραυτα = παρ ̓ αὐτά, sc. τὰ πράγματα) [in LXX: Psaumes 70:3, Tob.4:14 * ;] 
__1. immediately. 
__2. C. subst., to express brief duration (cf. ἡ π. λαμπρότης, Thuc., ii, 64), momentary, for a moment: 2 Corinthiens 4:17.†

G3911.def:
παρα-φέρω 
[in LXX: 1 Rois 21:13 (14) (הָלַל hithpo.), and as seel. 2* ;] 
__1. to bring to, set before, esp. of food (Hdt., al.). 
__2. to take or carry away: with accusative of thing(s), before ἀπό, Marc 14:36, Luc 22:42; pass., before ὑπό, Ju 12; metaphorically, pass., with dative, Hébreux 13:9.†

G3912.def:
παρα-φρονέω
(ιαρά, φρήν), [in LXX: Zacharie 7:11 (סָרַר)* ;] 
to be beside oneself, be deranged: 2 Corinthiens 11:23.†

G3913.def:
παρα-φρονία, -ας, ἡ 
= cl. παραφροσύνη, 
madness: 2 Pierre 2:16.†

G3914.def:
παρα-χειμάζω 
to winter at a place: before εἰς, Actes 27:12; ἐν, Actes 28:11; πρὸς ὑμᾶς, 1 Corinthiens 16:6; ἐκεῖ, Tite 3:12.†

G3915.def:
παρα-χειμασία, -ας, ἡ
(παρα-χειμάζω) 
a wintering: Actes 27:12 (Polyb., al.).†

G3916.def:
παραχρῆμα 
adv. (= παρὰ τὸ χρῆμα), [in LXX: Nombres 6:9 12:4, Ésaïe 29:5 30:13 (פִּתְאוֹם), etc. ;] 
on the spot, forthwith, instantly: Matthieu 21:19-20, Luc 1:64 4:39 5:25 8:44, 47 8:55 13:13 18:43 19:11 22:60, Actes 3:7 5:10 12:23 13:11 16:26, 33 (on the usage in Mt, Lk, see Dalman, Words, 28 f.).†

G3917.def:
πάρδαλις, -εως, ἡ 
[in LXX for נָמֵר, Cantique des cantiques 4:8, Osée 13:7, Ésaïe 11:6, al. ;] 
a panther, leopard: Apocalypse 13:2.†

G3919.def:
παρ-εισ-άγω 
__1. to lead in by one's side, bring forward, introduce. 
__2. In late writers, to introduce or bring in secretly: 2 Pierre 2:1.†

G3920.def:
παρ-είσ-ακτος, -ον
(παρεισάγω), 
brought in secretly (as spies or traitors) : Galates 2:4.†

G3921.def:
παρ-εισ-δύω
(also -δύνω), 
to slip in secretly, steal in: παρεισεδύησαν (vulgar aor.; pass. for act., El., § 19, 2), Ju 4 (cf. also MM, xix).†

G3922.def:
παρ-εισ-έρχομαι 
__1. to come in beside or by the way: Romains 5:20. 
__2. to come in secretly, steal in: Galates 2:4.†

G3923.def:
παρ-εισ-φέρω 
to bring in or supply besides: σπουδὴν π. (late Gk. for cl. σ. ποιεῖσθαι; cf. Deiss., BS, 361), 2 Pierre 1:5.†

G3924.def:
παρ-εκτός = cl. παρέκ, -έξ, 
[in Aq.: Deutéronome 1:36; Al., Lévitique 23:38 * ;] 
__1. as adv., besides, in addition: τὰ π. (sc. γινόμενα), 2 Corinthiens 11:28. 
__2. As prep. with genitive, except: Matthieu 5:32 19:9 (WH, mg., R, mg.), Actes 26:29.†

G3926.def:
παρ-εν-οχλέω, -ῶ
(cf. ἐνοχλέω), [in LXX for לָאָה hi. (Michée 6:3), etc. ;] 
to annoy concerning a matter (παρά): with dative of person(s), Actes 15:19.†

G3927.def:
παρ-επί-δημος, -ον
(see: ἐπιδημέω), [in LXX: Genèse 23:4, Psaumes 39:12 (תּוֹשָׁב)* ;] 
sojourning in a strange place; as subst., ὁ π., a sojourner: of Christians, 1 Pierre 1:1; ξένοι καὶ π., Hébreux 11:13; πάροικοι καὶ π., 1 Pierre 2:11 (see Deiss., BS, 149).†

G3929.def:
πάρεσις, -εως, ἡ
(παρίημι), 
__1. a letting go, dismissal. 
__2. prætermission, passing by (of debt or sin) : Romains 3:25†
SYN.: ἄφεσις, q.v

G3930.def:
παρ-έχω 
[in LXX: Psaumes 30:7 (עָמַד hi.), etc. ;] 
__I. Active voice., 
__1. to furnish, provide, supply; with ref. to incorporeal things, to afford, show, give, cause: with accusative, Actes 22:2, 1 Timothée 1:4; with accusative and dative, Matthieu 26:10, Marc 14:6, Luc 11:7 18:5, Actes 16:16 17:31 28:2, Galates 6:17, 1 Timothée 6:17. 
__2. to present, offer: with accusative and dative, Luc 6:29; with prop. reflex. and accusative pred., to show or present oneself (see infr., and cf. B1., § 55, 1). 
__II. Middle voice., 
__1. to supply, furnish or display of one's own part: with accusative and dative, Luc 7:4, Actes 19:24, Colossiens 4:1. 
__2. In late writers, with prop. reflex. and accusative pred. (= act. ut supr.), to show or present oneself (Xen., FlJ, al.; cf. M, Pr., 248; Deiss., BS, 254) : Tite 2:7.†

G3931.def:
παρηγορία, -ας, ἡ
(παρηγορέω, to address, exhort, console) [in LXX: 4Ma.5:12 4Mac 6:1 * ;] 
__1. an address, exhortation (LXX, ll. with). 
__2. comfort, consolation: Colossiens 4:11.†

G3932.def:
παρθενία, -ας, ἡ
(παρθένος), [in LXX: Jérémie 3:4 (נָעוּר), Sir.15:2 42:10, 4Ma.18:8 * ;] 
virginity: Luc 2:36.†

G3933.def:
παρθένος, -ου, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for בְּתוּלָה, Exode 22:16 (15), Job 31:1, Ésaïe 23:4, al.; also for נַעַר, נַעֲרָה, Genèse 24:14, 16 24:55 34:3, and for עַלְמָה, Genèse 24:43, Ésaïe 7:14 ;] 
a maiden, virgin: Matthieu 1:23 (LXX) Matthieu 25:1, 7 25:11 Luc 1:27, Actes 21:9, 1 Corinthiens 7:25 ff, 2 Corinthiens 11:2; masc., of chaste persons (CIG, 8784 b) : Apocalypse 14:4.†

G3935.def:
παρ-ίημι 
[in LXX: Jérémie 4:31 (פָּרַשׂ pi.), etc. ;] 
__1. to pass by or over, let alone, disregard: Luc 11:42. 
__2. to relax, loosen; pass., to be relaxed, weakened, exhausted: παρειμένας χεῖρας, Hébreux 12:12 (LXX ἀνειμ-).†

G3936.def:
παρ-ίστημι 
[in LXX for עָמַד, etc. ;] 
__I. Transitive verb. in present tense., imperfect., future tense., 1 aorist.; 
__1. to place beside, present, provide: with accusative, Actes 9:41 23:24, 2 Corinthiens 4:14, Colossiens 1:28; with accusative and dative, Matthieu 26:53, Luc 2:22, Actes 1:3 23:33, 1 Corinthiens 8:8; before accusative pred., Romains 6:13, 16 (late pres., παριστάνετε), Romains 6:19 12:1, 2 Corinthiens 11:2, Éphésiens 5:27, Colossiens 1:22, 2 Timothée 2:15. 
__2. to present to the mind (cl.) : by argument, to prove (Xen., FlJ, al.), with accusative, Actes 24:13. 
__II. Intransitive. in perfect., pluperfect., 2 aorist.; 
__1. to stand by or beside one : with dative of person(s), Actes 1:10 9:39 23:2 27:23; ptcp., Marc 14:47, 69-70 15:35, 39 Jean 18:22 19:26. 
__2. to appear: with nom. pred., before ἐνώπιον, Actes 4:10; with dative of person(s), Actes 27:24; so fut. mid. (of. LS, see word, B, ii, 2), Romains 14:10. 
__3. to be at hand, be present, have come: Actes 4:26 (LXX); of servants in attendance, ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ, Luc 1:19; absol., οἱ παρεστῶτες, Luc 19:24; before αὐτῷ, Actes 23:2, 4; of time, Marc 4:29 
__4. to stand by for help or defence (Hom., Dem., Xen., al.): with dative of person(s), Romains 16:2, 2 Timothée 4:17.†

G3938.def:
πάρ-οδος, -ου, ἡ 
[in LXX: Genèse 38:14 (דֶּרֶךְ), etc. ;] 
a passing or passage: ἐν π., in passing, 1 Corinthiens 16:7.†

G3939.def:
παρ-οικέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for גּוּר, also for יָשַׁב, שָׁכַן ] 
in cl., to dwell beside (with accusative), among (with dative) or near by (absol.). In late writers, to dwell in a place as a πάροικος (which see) or stranger: Luc 24:18, Hébreux 11:9.†

G3940.def:
παρ-οικία, -ας, ἡ
(παροικέω, which see), [in LXX: Esther 8:35 (גּוֹלָה), Psaumes 34:4 55:15 119:54 120:5, La 2:22 (מָגוֹר; and cogn. forms), Habacuc 3:16, I Esther 5:7, Jdth.5:9, Wis.19:10, Sir prol. Sir.1:26 16:8 41:5 44:6, 3Ma.6:36 3Mac 7:19 * ;] 
a sojourning: Actes 13:17, 1 Pierre 1:17.†

G3941.def:
άρ-οικος, -ον 
[in LXX chiefly for גֵּר, תּוֹשָׁב ;] 
__1. in cl. Attic, dwelling near, neighbouring; as subst., a neighbour. 
__2. In late writers (LXX, Philo) and in Iuser. (Deiss., BS, 227 f.; Kennedy, Sources, 102), foreign, alien; as subst., an alien, a sojourner: Actes 7:6 (LXX), Actes 7:29; metapb., ξένοι καὶ π. (opposite to συμπολίτης), Éphésiens 2:19; π. καὶ παρεπιδήμους (which see), 1 Pierre 2:11 (see Lft. on Clem. Rom., 1 Co., § 1).†

G3942.def:
παροιμία, -ας, ἡ
(πάροιμος, by the way), [in LXX. Pr title Proverbes 1:1 25:1, (מָשַׁל) subscr., Sir.6:35 8:8 18:29 39:3 47:17 * ;] 
__1. a wayside saying (Hesych.; see LS, see word), a byword, maxim, proverb: 2 Pierre 2:22. 
__2. In NT, of figurative discourse (as מָשַׁל, Ésaïe 14:4, al.), a parable, allegory: Jean 10:6 16:25, 29 (see Abbott, Essays, 82 ff.).†
SYN.: παραβολή, q.v

G3943.def:
πάρ-οινος, -ον 
= cl., παροινικός (παρά, οἶνος), 
given to wine, drunken: 1 Timothée 3:3, Tite 1:7.†

G3944.def:
παρ-οίχομαι 
to have passed by; of time, to be gone by: ἐν τ. παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς, Actes 14:16.†

G3945.def:
παρ-ομοιάζω 
to be like: with dative, Matthieu 23:27.†

G3947.def:
παρ-οξύνω 
[in LXX for נָאַץ, קָצַף, רָגַז, etc. ;] 
__1. primarily, but never so in cl., to sharpen (μάχαιραν, Deutéronome 32:41, שָׁנַן). 
__2. Metaphorical, as always in cl., 
__(a) to spur on, stimulate (Arist., Xen., al.); 
__(b) to provoke, rouse to anger (Deutéronome 9:7, 18, Psaumes 106:29, al.) : pass., Actes 17:16, 1 Corinthiens 13:5.†

G3948.def:
παροξυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(παροξύνω), [in LXX: Deutéronome 29:28, Jérémie 32:37 (קֶצֶף)* ;] 
__1. stimulation, provocation: π. ἀγάπης, Hébreux 10:14. 
__2. irritation: Actes 15:39.†

G3949.def:
παρ-οργίζω 
[in LXX chiefly for כַּעַס hi. ;] 
(in cl., passive only), to provoke to anger: Romains 10:19 (LXX), Éphésiens 6:4.†

G3950.def:
παρ-οργισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(παροργίζω), [in LXX: 3Ki.15:30, 4Ki.23:26 (כַּעַס); 4Ki.19:3, Néhémie 9:18, 26 (נְאָצָה); Jérémie 21:5 A (קֶצֶף) * ;] 
irritation ("distinguished from ὀργή as implying a less permanent state"; ICC, Eph., 140; and see Tr., Syn., § xxxvii) : Éphésiens 4:26.†

G3951.def:
παρ-οτρύνω 
to urge on, stir up: with accusative of person(s), Actes 13:50 (find., Hipp., and late writers).†

G3952.def:
παρ-ουσία, -ας, ἡ 
[in LXX: Néhémie 2:6 A, Jdth.10:18, 2Ma.8:12 2Mac 15:21, 3Ma.3:17 * ;] 
__1. usually in cl., a being present, presence: 1 Corinthiens 16:17, 2 Corinthiens 10:10; opposite to ἀπουσία, Philippiens 2:12 (cf. 2Ma.15:21). 
__2. a coming, arrival, advent (Soph., Eur., Thuc., al., see LS, see word; so Jth, l.with, 2Ma.8:12) : 2 Corinthiens 7:6-7, Philippiens 1:26, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:9; in late writers (see M, Th., 145 ff.; MM, xix; LAE, 372 ff.) as technical term for the visit of a king; hence, in NT, specif. of the Advent or Parousia of Christ : Matthieu 24:3, 27 24:37, 39, 1 Corinthiens 15:23, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:19 3:13 4:15 5:23, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:1 2:8, Jacques 5:7-8, 2 Pierre 1:16 3:4 3:12, 1 Jean 2:28.†

G3953.def:
παρ-οψίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(παρά, ὄψον; see: ὀψάριον), 
__1. a side-dish of dainties (Xen., al.). 
__2. In Comic poets and late prose, the dish itself on which the dainties are served: Matthieu 23:25-26 (In this sense it is condemned by the Atticists; see Rutherford, NPhr., 265 f.)†

G3954.def:
παρρησία, -ας, ἡ
(πᾶς + ῥῆσις, speech) [in LXX; Lévitique 26:13 (μετὰ π., קוֺמְמִיּוּת קוֹמְמִיּוּת), Proverbes 1:20 10:10, Wis.5:1, al. ;] 
__1. freedom of speech, plainness, openness, freedom in speaking (Eur., Plat., al.) : Actes 4:13, 2 Corinthiens 3:12; παρρησίᾳ, adverbially, freely, openly, plainly, Marc 8:32, Jean 7:13, 26 10:24 11:14 16:29 18:20; opposite to ἐν παροιμίαις, Jean 16:25; ἐν π., Éphésiens 6:19; μετὰ π., Actes 2:29 4:29, 31 28:31 
__2. In LXX (1Ma.4:18, Wis.5:1, al.), FlJ, and NT, also (from the absence of fear which accompanies freedom of speech), confidence, boldness: 2 Corinthiens 7:4, Philippiens 1:20, 1 Timothée 3:13; ἔχειν π., Éphésiens 3:12, Phm 8, Hébreux 3:6 10:19, 35, 1 Jean 2:28 Jn 3:21 Jn 4:17 Jn 5:14; μετὰ π., He 416; ἐν π., Colossiens 2:15; id. (as בפרהסיא in Rabbinic lit.; see Westc., Jo., i, 262), in public, Jean 7:4 and (without ἐν) Jean 11:54.†

G3955.def:
παρρησιάζομαι
(παρρησία), [in LXX: Job 22:26 (עָנַג hithp.), Psaumes 12:5 94:1, Proverbes 20:9, Cantique des cantiques 8:10, Sir.6:11 * ;] 
to speak freely or boldly, be bold in speech: Actes 9:27-28 13:46 14:3 18:26 19:8 26:26, Éphésiens 6:20, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:2.†

G3956.def:
πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν, genitive, παντός, πάσης, παντός, 
[in LXX chiefly for כֹּל ;] 
all, every. 
__I. As adj., 
__1. with subst. anarth., all, every, of every kind: Matthieu 3:10 4:23, Marc 9:49, Luc 4:37, Jean 2:1o, Actes 27:20, Romains 7:8, Apocalypse 18:17, al. mult.; pl., all, Actes 22:15, Romains 5:12, Hébreux 1:6, al.; of the highest degree, π. ἐξουσία (προθυμία, χαρά), Matthieu 28:18, Actes 17:11, Phi 2:29, al.; also the whole (though in this sense more frequently with art.), Matthieu 2:3, Actes 2:36, Romains 11:26. 
__2. C. art. (before the art., after the noun, or, denoting totality, between the art. and noun), all, whole: Matthieu 8:32 13:2, Marc 5:33, Luc 1:10, Actes 7:14, Romains 3:19, Galates 5:14, Éphésiens 4:16, al.; pl., Matthieu 2:4, Marc 4:13, Romains 1:5, al. 
__II. As pron., 
__1. masc. and fem., every one: Marc 9:49, Luc 16:16, Hébreux 2:9; before rel. pron., Matthieu 7:24, Actes 2:21, Galates 3:10, al.; with ptcp. (anarth.), Matthieu 13:19, Luc 11:4; with ptcp. (with art.), Matthieu 5:22, Marc 7:8, Luc 6:47, Jean 3:8, Romains 1:16, al.; pl., πάντες, absol., all, all men, Matthieu 10:22, Marc 13:13, Luc 20:38, Jean 1:7 3:26, 1 Corinthiens 8:1, al.; οἱ π. (collectively, as a definite whole), Romains 11:32, 1 Corinthiens 1:17, Éphésiens 4:13, al.; π. οἱ (ὅσοι), Matthieu 4:24, Marc 1:32, Luc 4:40, al. 
__2. Neut., 
__(a) sing., πᾶν, everything, all: πᾶν τό, with ptcp., 1 Corinthiens 10:25, 27, Éphésiens 5:13, 1 Jean 2:16 5:4 (sc. ὄν); πᾶν ὅ, Jean 17:2, Romains 14:23; collectively, of persons (Westc., in l.), Jean 6:37, 39; with prep., in adverbial phrases, διὰ παντός, always, Matthieu 18:10, al.; ἐν παντί, in everything, in every way, 2 Corinthiens 4:8, Phi 4:6, al.; 
__(b) pl., πάτνα, all things: absol., Jean 1:3, 1 Corinthiens 2:10, Hébreux 2:8, al.; of certain specified things, Marc 4:34, Luc 1:3, Romains 8:28, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:21, al.; accusative, πάντα, adverbially, wholly, in all things, in all respects, Actes 20:35, 1 Corinthiens 9:25, al.; with art., τὰ π., all things (a totality, as distinct from anarth. πάντα, all things severally; cf. Westc, Eph., 186f.), absol.: Romains 11:36, 1 Corinthiens 8:6, Éphésiens 3:9, Hébreux 1:3, al.; relatively, Marc 4:11, Actes 17:25, Romains 8:32, al.; πάντα, with ptcp., Matthieu 18:31, al.; πάντα ταῦτα (ταῦτα π.), Matthieu 6:32, 33, al.; πάντα, with prep, in adverbial phrases, πρὸ πάντων, above all things, Jacques 5:12, 1 Pierre 4:8; ἐν π́, in all things, in all ways, 1 Timothée 3:11, 1 Pierre 4:11, al.; κατὰ πάντα, in all respects, Actes 17:22, al. 
__3. C. neg., πᾶς οὐ (μή) = οὐδείς, see: οὐ and μή, and cf. M, Pr., 245f.

G3957.def:
πάσχα, τό indecl. (Aram. טַּסְחָא), 
[in LXX for פֶּסַח ;] 
__1. the festival of the Passover: Matthieu 26:2, Marc 14:1, Luc 22:1, Jean 2:13, 23 6:4 11:55 12:1 18:39 19:14, Actes 12:4, Hébreux 11:28; .ἡ ἐορτὴ τοῦ π., Luc 2:41, Jean 13:1. 
__2. By meton., 
__(a) the paschal supper: ἑτοιμάζειν τὸ π., Matthieu 26:19, Marc 14:16, Luc 22:8, 13; ποιεῖν τό π., Matthieu 26:18; 
__(b) the pasohal lamb: θύειν τό π. (Exode 12:21), Marc 14:12, Luc 22:7; of Christ, 1 Corinthiens 5:7; φαγεῖν τὸ π. (lamb or supper), Matthieu 26:17, Marc 14:12, 14, Luc 22:11, 15, Jean 18:28 (cf. 2 Chroniques 30:17).†

G3959.def:
Πάταρα, -ων, τὰ 
Patara, a maritime city of Lycia: Actes 21:1.†

G3960.def:
πατάσσω 
[in LXX chiefly and very frequently for נָכָה hi., also for נָגַף, etc. ;] 
__1. in Hom., intrans., to beat (of the heart). 
__2. Trans. = πλήσσω, to strike, smite: absol., ἐν μαχαίρᾳ, Luc 22:49; with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 26:51, Luc 22:50; with accusative of thing(s), Actes 12:7; of a deadly blow, Matthieu 26:31, Marc 14:27, Actes 7:24. Metaphorical, of disease: Actes 12:23, Apocalypse 11:6 19:15.†

G3961.def:
πατέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX for דָּרַךְ, etc. ;] 
__1. intrans., to tread, walk: before ἐπάνω ὄφεων κ.τ.λ. (figuratively), Luc 10:19 (cf. Psaumes 91:13). 
__2. Trans., to tread on, trample: τ. ληνόν, Apocalypse 14:20 19:15 (cf. Juges 9:27, La 1:15, al.); of the desecration of Jerusalem by its enemies, Luc 21:24, Apocalypse 11:2 (cf. κατα-, περι-, ἐν-περι-πατέω).†

G3963.def:
Πάτμος, -ου, ἡ 
Patmos, an island in the Ægean Sea: Apocalypse 1:9.†

G3964.def:
πατρολῴας (-αλῴας, Rec.; in cl. -αλοίας, see Bl., § 3, 3; 6, 2, and cf. μητρολῴας), -ου, ὁ 
(πατήρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite), 
__(a) a parricide: 1 Timothée 1:9 (Av, R, txt.); 
__(b) a smiter of his father : ib. (R, mg.).†

G3965.def:
πατριά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(πατήρ), [in LXX chiefly for אָב, Exode 6:14, al., also for מִשְׁפָּחָה, Exode 6:15, 4Ki.14:7, Psaumes 22:27, al. ;] 
__1. lineage, ancestry (Hdt.). 
__2. = πάτρα (more common in cl.), a family or tribe (so sometimes in Hdt., in LXX of related people, in a sense narrower than φυλή and wider than οἶκος; see Exode 12:3, Nombres 32:28): Luc 2:4; in a wider sense (1 Chroniques 16:28, Psaumes 22:27), Actes 3:25" (LXX) Éphésiens 3:15.†

G3966.def:
πατριάρχης, -ου, ὁ
(πατριά, ἄρχω), [in LXX: 1 Chroniques 24:31 (אָב), 2 Chroniques 19:8 26:12 (אָב רֹאשׁ), 1 Chroniques 27:12 (שַׂר), 2 Chroniques 23:20 (מֵאָה שַׂר), 4Ma.7:19 4Mac 16:25 * ;] 
a patriarch: Actes 2:29 7:8-9, Hébreux 7:4.†

G3967.def:
πατρικίς, -ή, -όν
(πατήρ), [in LXX for אָב, Genèse 50:8, al. ;] 
paternal, ancestral: Galates 1:14.†

G3968.def:
πατρίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(πατήρ), [in LXX chiefly for מוֹלֶדֶת ;] 
prop. poët. fern. of πάτριος, of one's fathers; as subst., ἡ π. = πάτρα, fatherland, country, home, native place: Actes 18:27, WH, mg., Hébreux 11:14; of one's own town, Matthieu 13:54, 57, Marc 6:1, 4, Luc 4:23-24, Jean 4:44.†

G3970.def:
πατρο-παρά-δοτος, -ον
(πατήρ, παραδίδωμι), 
handed down from one's fathers, inherited: 1 Pierre 1:18 (Diod., al.).†

G3971.def:
πατρῷος, -α, -ον
(πατήρ), [in LXX: Proverbes 27:10 (אָב), Esther 7:5, 2 -4Ma.12:1-19 * ;] 
of one's fathers, received from one's fathers: Actes 22:3 24:14 28:17.†

G3972G.def:
Παῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. Paulus), 
__1. Sergius Paulus: Actes 13:7. 
__2. the Apostle Paul (cf. Σαῦλος): Actes 13:9, and frequently throughout Ac., Romains 1:1, 1 Corinthiens 1:1, al., 2 Pierre 3:15.

G3972H.def:
Παῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. Paulus), 
__1. Sergius Paulus: Actes 13:7. 
__2. the Apostle Paul (cf. Σαῦλος): Actes 13:9, and frequently throughout Ac., Romains 1:1, 1 Corinthiens 1:1, al., 2 Pierre 3:15.

G3973.def:
παύω 
[in LXX for כָּלָה pi., etc. ;] 
to make to cease, restrain, hinder: with accusative of thing(s), before ἀπό 1 Pierre 3:10 (LXX). Mid., to cease, leave off: Luc 8:24 11:1, Actes 20:1, 1 Corinthiens 13:8; with ptcp., Luc 5:4, Actes 5:42 6:13 13:10 20:31 21:32, Éphésiens 1:16, Colossiens 1:9, Hébreux 10:2; with genitive, ἀμαρτίας, 1 Pierre 4:1 (WH, mg., R, txt.); with dative, ib. (WH, txt., R, mg.).†

G3974.def:
Πάφος, -ου, ἡ 
Paphos, a city in Cyprus: Actes 13:6, 13 †

G3975.def:
παχύνω
(παχύς, thick) [in LXX: Deutéronome 32:15, Ésaïe 6:10 (שָׁמֵן), al. ;] 
to thicken, fatten; pass., to grow fat. Metaphorical, to make dull or stupid (τ. ψυχάς, Rut.); pass., to wax gross: ἡ καρδία„ Matthieu 13:15, Actes 28:27" (LXX) .†

G3976.def:
πέδη, -ης, ἡ
(πέζα, the instep), [in LXX for נְחֹשֶׁת, etc. ;] 
a fetter: Marc 5:4, Luc 8:29.†

G3977.def:
πεδινός, -ή, -όν
(πεδίον, a plain), [in LXX chiefly for שְׁפֵלָה (ἡ π.) ;] 
level, plain: Luc 6:17.†

G3978.def:
πεζεύω
(πεζός) 
to travel on foot or by land: Actes 20:13.†

G3979.def:
πεζός, -ή, -όν
(πούς), [in LXX for רַגְלִי ;] 
__1. on foot: Matthieu 14:13 (WH, mg., R, txt.). 
__2. Opp. to going by sea, by land: Matthieu 14:13 (WH, mg., R, mg.). 
__3. As adv., πεζῇ (sc. ὁδῷ), on foot or by land: Mt 1413 (WH, txt.), Marc 6:33.†

G3980.def:
πειθαρχέω, -ῶ
(πείθομαι, ἀρχή) [in LXX: Dan LXX 7:27 (שְׁמַע), Sir.33:28, I Esther 8:94 * ;] 
to obey one in authority, be obedient: Tite 3:1; with dative, Actes 27:21; θεῷ, Actes 5:29, 32.†

G3981.def:
πειθός (πιθός, WH), -ή, -όν 
(πείθω), = cl. πιθανός, 
persuasive: 1 Corinthiens 2:4 (not found elsewhere).†

G3982.def:
πείθω, 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּטַח בֶּטַח, its parts and derivatives ;] 
__(i) Active; 
__1. trans., to apply persuasion ("conative" in pres.; see M, Pr., 147), to prevail upon or win over, persuade: absol., Matthieu 28:14, Actes 19:26; before περί, with genitive of thing(s), Actes 19:8; with accusative of person(s), Actes 12:20 14:19 18:4, 2 Corinthiens 5:11, Galates 1:10; τ. καρδίας ἡμῶν, 1 Jean 3:19; with accusative before περί, Actes 28:23; with accusative and inf., Actes 13:43 26:28 (see Field, Notes, 141 ff.); with accusative before ἵνα (Plut.), Matthieu 27:20. 
__2. Intrans., 2 pf. πέποιθα with Pres. sense (see M, Pr., 147, 154; Bl., § 59, 2): to trust, be confident, have confidence: with accusative and inf., Romains 2:19; with accusative ref. (see Ellic., in l) : Philippiens 1:6, 25; with dative, Philippiens 1:14, Phm 21; ἑαυτῷ, with inf., 2 Corinthiens 10:7; before ἐν, Philippiens 3:3-4; ἐν κυρίῳ ὅτι, Philippiens 2:24; ἐπί, with dative, Matthieu 27:43 (WH, mg.), Marc 10:24 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Luc 11:22 18:9, 2 Corinthiens 1:9, Hébreux 2:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Matthieu 27:43 (with dative, WH, mg.); id. before ὅτι, 2 Corinthiens 2:3, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:4 (see Lft., Notes, 127); εἰς, with accusative of person(s) before ὅτι, Galates 5:10. 
(ii) Pass. and mid.; 
__1. to be persuaded, believe (see M, Pr., 158) : absol., Luc 16:31, Actes 17:4 21:14, Hébreux 13:18; with dative, Actes 28:24; with accusative and inf., Actes 26:26; so also pf., πέπεισμαι, πεπεισμένος εἰμί: with accusative ref. before περί, Hébreux 6:9; with accusative and inf., Luc 20:6; ὅτι, Romains 8:38, 2 Timothée 1:5 1:12; id. with ἐν κυρίῳ, Romains 14:14; περί, with genitive before ὅτι, Romains 15:14. 
__2. to listen to, obey: with dative of person(s), Actes 5:36-37, 40 23:21 27:11, Romains 2:8, Galates 5:7, Hébreux 13:17, Jacques 3:3 (cf. ἀνα-πείθω).†
Πειθώ, -οῦς, ἡ 
__1. Peitho, Persuasion (as a goddess). 
__2. per­suasion: ἐν πειθοῖ (so Orig., Eus. and some cursives in 1 Corinthiens 2:4 for πειθός, which see).†

G3983.def:
πεινάω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for = רָעֵב ;] 
to hunger, be hungry: Matthieu 4:2 12:1, 3 21:18 25:35, 37 25:42, 44, Marc 2:25 11:12, Luc 1:53 4:2 6:3, Romains 12:20" (LXX), 1 Corinthiens 4:11 11:21 11:34 Philippiens 4:12, Apocalypse 7:16; metaphorically, Matthieu 5:6, Luc 6:21, 25, Jean 6:35.†

G3984.def:
πεῖρα, -ας, ἡ
(πειράω), [in LXX: Deutéronome 28:56 (π. λαμβάνειν, נָסָה pi.) Deutéronome 33:8 (מַסָּה), Wis.18:20, 25, 2Ma.8:9, 4Ma.8:1 * ;] 
trial, experiment; π. λαμβάνειν, to make trial, have experience of: Hébreux 11:29, 36 (for exx., see Field, Notes, 232 f.).†

G3986G.def:
πειρασμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(πειράζω), [in LXX for מַסָּה, עִנְיָן ;] 
__1. = πεῖρα, an experiment Diosc.). 
__2. a trial, of ethical purpose and effect, whether good or evil (see Hort on Jacques 1:13) 
__(a) in good or neutral sense: Galates 4:14, Jacques 1:12, 1 Pierre 4:12; esp. of afflictions sent by God (Deutéronome 7:19, Sir.21:1-28, al.): 2 Pierre 2:9, Apocalypse 3:10; pl., Luc 22:28, Actes 20:19, Jacques 1:2, 1 Pierre 1:6; 
__(b) of trial regarded as leading to sin, temptation: Luc 8:13, 1 Corinthiens 10:13, 1 Timothée 6:9; of the temptation of Jesus by the devil, Luc 4:13; εἰσφέρειν (ἔρχεσθαι, εἰσέρχ-) εἰς π., Matthieu 6:13 26:41, Marc 14:38, Luc 11:4 22:40, 46; 
__(with) of the testing or challenge of God by man (see: πειράζω, 3, with) : Hébreux 3:8 (LXX: Psaumes 95:9, where κατα τ. ἡμέραν πειρασμοῦ = מַסָּה the day of Massah).†
SYN.: δοκίμιον

G3986H.def:
πειρασμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(πειράζω), [in LXX for מַסָּה, עִנְיָן ;] 
__1. = πεῖρα, an experiment Diosc.). 
__2. a trial, of ethical purpose and effect, whether good or evil (see Hort on Jacques 1:13) 
__(a) in good or neutral sense: Galates 4:14, Jacques 1:12, 1 Pierre 4:12; esp. of afflictions sent by God (Deutéronome 7:19, Sir.21:1-28, al.): 2 Pierre 2:9, Apocalypse 3:10; pl., Luc 22:28, Actes 20:19, Jacques 1:2, 1 Pierre 1:6; 
__(b) of trial regarded as leading to sin, temptation: Luc 8:13, 1 Corinthiens 10:13, 1 Timothée 6:9; of the temptation of Jesus by the devil, Luc 4:13; εἰσφέρειν (ἔρχεσθαι, εἰσέρχ-) εἰς π., Matthieu 6:13 26:41, Marc 14:38, Luc 11:4 22:40, 46; 
__(with) of the testing or challenge of God by man (see: πειράζω, 3, with) : Hébreux 3:8 (LXX: Psaumes 95:9, where κατα τ. ἡμέραν πειρασμοῦ = מַסָּה the day of Massah).†
SYN.: δοκίμιον

G3987.def:
πειράω more commonly as depon., πειράομαι, 
[in LXX for נָסָה ;] 
to try, attempt: Actes 26:21.†

G3988.def:
πεισμονή, -ῆς, ἡ
(πείθω), 
persuasion: Galates 5:8.†
πείθω, 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּטַח בֶּטַח, its parts and derivatives ;] 
__(i) Active; 
__1. trans., to apply persuasion ("conative" in pres.; see M, Pr., 147), to prevail upon or win over, persuade: absol., Matthieu 28:14, Actes 19:26; before περί, with genitive of thing(s), Actes 19:8; with accusative of person(s), Actes 12:20 14:19 18:4, 2 Corinthiens 5:11, Galates 1:10; τ. καρδίας ἡμῶν, 1 Jean 3:19; with accusative before περί, Actes 28:23; with accusative and inf., Actes 13:43 26:28 (see Field, Notes, 141 ff.); with accusative before ἵνα (Plut.), Matthieu 27:20. 
__2. Intrans., 2 pf. πέποιθα with Pres. sense (see M, Pr., 147, 154; Bl., § 59, 2): to trust, be confident, have confidence: with accusative and inf., Romains 2:19; with accusative ref. (see Ellic., in l) : Philippiens 1:6, 25; with dative, Philippiens 1:14, Phm 21; ἑαυτῷ, with inf., 2 Corinthiens 10:7; before ἐν, Philippiens 3:3-4; ἐν κυρίῳ ὅτι, Philippiens 2:24; ἐπί, with dative, Matthieu 27:43 (WH, mg.), Marc 10:24 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Luc 11:22 18:9, 2 Corinthiens 1:9, Hébreux 2:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Matthieu 27:43 (with dative, WH, mg.); id. before ὅτι, 2 Corinthiens 2:3, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:4 (see Lft., Notes, 127); εἰς, with accusative of person(s) before ὅτι, Galates 5:10. 
(ii) Pass. and mid.; 
__1. to be persuaded, believe (see M, Pr., 158) : absol., Luc 16:31, Actes 17:4 21:14, Hébreux 13:18; with dative, Actes 28:24; with accusative and inf., Actes 26:26; so also pf., πέπεισμαι, πεπεισμένος εἰμί: with accusative ref. before περί, Hébreux 6:9; with accusative and inf., Luc 20:6; ὅτι, Romains 8:38, 2 Timothée 1:5 1:12; id. with ἐν κυρίῳ, Romains 14:14; περί, with genitive before ὅτι, Romains 15:14. 
__2. to listen to, obey: with dative of person(s), Actes 5:36-37, 40 23:21 27:11, Romains 2:8, Galates 5:7, Hébreux 13:17, Jacques 3:3 (cf. ἀνα-πείθω).†

G3989.def:
πέλαγος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX: 2Ma.5:21, 4Ma.7:1 * ;] 
the deep sea, the deep, the sea: Actes 27:5; τὸ π. τῆς θαλάσσης, Matthieu 18:6 
SYN.: θαλάσσα (which see); and cf. ἄβυσσος

G3990.def:
πελεκίζω
(πέλεκυς, a battle-axe), 
to out off with an axe, esp. to behead: with accusative, Apocalypse 20:4 (Polyb., al.).†

G3991.def:
πέμπτος, -η, -ον 
[in LXX for חֲמִישִׁי and cognate forms ;] 
fifth: Apocalypse 6:9 9:1 16:10 21:20.†

G3993.def:
πένης, -ητος, ὁ
(πένομαι, to work for one's daily bread), [in LXX for אֶבְיוֹן, עָנִי, דַּל, etc. ;] 
one who works for his living, a labourer, a poor man: 2 Corinthiens 9:9.†
SYN.: πτωχός, properly a beggar and implying deeper poverty than π. (see Tr., Syn., § xxxvi, Abbott, Essays, 78)

G3994.def:
πενθερά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(fem. of πενθερός), [in LXX for חֲמוֹת ;] 
a mother-in-law: Matthieu 8:14 10:35, Marc 1:30, Luc 4:38 12:53.†

G3995.def:
πενθερός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for חָם, Genèse 38:13, al.; also for חָתַן, Juges 1:16 A ;] 
a father-in-law: Jean 18:13.†

G3997.def:
πένθος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for אֵבֶל ;] 
mourning: Jacques 4:9, Apocalypse 18:7-8 21:4.†

G3998.def:
πενιχρός, -ά, -όν
(πένομαι, see: πένης) [in LXX: Exode 22:25 (עָנִי), Proverbes 28:15 29:7 (דַּל) * ;] 
chiefly in Comic poets and late prose (but Plato, Rep., 578 A), = πένης, 
needy, poor: Luc 21:2 (for ex. in π., see MM, xix).†
